scenes.tts: A circuit is built in development. If a child is born without one of its proteins, is the circuit wrong for good?
scenes.visual: Title card: Built, Then Kept. A single schematic synapse assembles: neurexin meets neuroligin, a scaffold appears, receptors cluster. A question mark.
scenes.narration: A circuit is built in development. If a child is born without one of its proteins, is the circuit wrong for good?

scenes.tts: Autism is diagnosed from behaviour, not from a gene, blood or scan test.
scenes.visual: A clinician's checklist of behaviours beside a crossed-out test tube, scanner and D N A icon.
scenes.narration: Autism is diagnosed from behaviour, not from a gene, blood or scan test.

scenes.tts: Yet about a hundred genes now have strong evidence for a role in autism.
scenes.visual: A cloud of about one hundred gene labels drifts, then begins to sort.
scenes.narration: Yet about a hundred genes now have strong evidence for a role in autism.

scenes.tts: Many fall into three jobs. Some build and hold the synapse.
scenes.visual: The same synapse. Tag 1, scaffold colour: build and hold the synapse. Neurexin, neuroligin and a scaffold glow.
scenes.narration: Many fall into three jobs. Some build and hold the synapse.

scenes.tts: Some set how much protein a synapse makes.
scenes.visual: Tag 2, translation colour: ribosomes in the dendrite near the synapse light up.
scenes.narration: Some set how much protein a synapse makes.

scenes.tts: And some set which genes the neuron uses.
scenes.visual: Tag 3, nucleus colour: the cell nucleus glows, sending messages out toward the dendrite.
scenes.narration: And some set which genes the neuron uses.

scenes.tts: The three jobs seem to meet at the synapse. Each can change what it is made of, and how strongly it responds.
scenes.visual: All three tags point to the one synapse. Label: three ways that can change one synapse.
scenes.narration: The three jobs seem to meet at the synapse. Each can change what it is made of, and how strongly it responds.

scenes.tts: Much of building happens early, in windows that close. Picture a mouse born without one synapse protein, with symptoms by young adulthood.
scenes.visual: A developmental timeline; a shaded building window closes. A mouse icon appears, with a symptom marker at young adulthood.
scenes.narration: Much of building happens early, in windows that close. Picture a mouse born without one synapse protein, with symptoms by young adulthood.

scenes.tts: One history: the protein was needed to build the circuit. The circuit was built wrong, and the window has closed.
scenes.visual: Panel A: a miswired circuit inside the closed window. Label: built wrong.
scenes.narration: One history: the protein was needed to build the circuit. The circuit was built wrong, and the window has closed.

scenes.tts: Another history: the circuit was built well enough. But it cannot run without the protein.
scenes.visual: Panel B: a correctly wired circuit with dim, flickering activity. Label: built, not kept.
scenes.narration: Another history: the circuit was built well enough. But it cannot run without the protein.

scenes.tts: The symptoms look the same either way.
scenes.visual: Both panels lead to the same symptom marker.
scenes.narration: The symptoms look the same either way.

scenes.tts: Predict. You can switch the gene on or off at any age. Which two late experiments would tell these histories apart?
scenes.visual: Text on screen: Predict. Two late experiments? A switch icon with an age dial.
scenes.narration: Predict. You can switch the gene on or off at any age. Which two late experiments would tell these histories apart?

scenes.tts: First, put the gene back after symptoms begin.
scenes.visual: An empty grid appears. Column 1: restore late.
scenes.narration: First, put the gene back after symptoms begin.

scenes.tts: Second, take it away from a typical mouse, after its circuit is built.
scenes.visual: Column 2: delete late. Rows: build only, upkeep only, both. All cells empty.
scenes.narration: Second, take it away from a typical mouse, after its circuit is built.

scenes.tts: If the protein was needed only to build, and the damage cannot be repaired, both tests do nothing.
scenes.visual: Row build only fills: restore late, no; delete late, no. Small note: if the damage cannot be repaired.
scenes.narration: If the protein was needed only to build, and the damage cannot be repaired, both tests do nothing.

scenes.tts: If it keeps the circuit running, restoring it helps, and removing it harms.
scenes.visual: Row upkeep only fills: yes; yes.
scenes.narration: If it keeps the circuit running, restoring it helps, and removing it harms.

scenes.tts: If it does both, restoring it may help fully, partly or not at all. Removing it still harms.
scenes.visual: Row both fills: restore late, none, partial or full; delete late, yes.
scenes.narration: If it does both, restoring it may help fully, partly or not at all. Removing it still harms.

scenes.tts: A failed rescue is hard to read: the gene may have come back in too few cells, at the wrong level or too briefly, or the window may have closed. Deletion asks whether the adult circuit still needs the gene. You need both tests.
scenes.visual: A brain section with the restored gene in a few scattered cells. Labels: too few cells? wrong level? too short? window closed? Footnote under the grid: assumes the gene really comes back, or goes, in enough cells.
scenes.narration: A failed rescue is hard to read: the gene may have come back in too few cells, at the wrong level or too briefly, or the window may have closed. Deletion asks whether the adult circuit still needs the gene. You need both tests.

scenes.tts: Carry one idea through this lesson. Built, then kept. A synapse gene can be needed to build a circuit, to keep it running, or both.
scenes.visual: Guiding-idea card: Built, then kept. Build, keep, or both. Two late tests, read trait by trait.
scenes.narration: Carry one idea through this lesson. Built, then kept. A synapse gene can be needed to build a circuit, to keep it running, or both.

scenes.tts: Takeaway: restore the gene late, and delete it late. One asks if a trait can recover. The other asks if the adult circuit still needs it.
scenes.visual: Closing card: the filled grid, with the two column headings highlighted. Labels: can the trait recover? Does the adult circuit still need it? Neither rules out building.
scenes.narration: Takeaway: restore the gene late, and delete it late. One asks if a trait can recover. The other asks if the adult circuit still needs it.
